title: Manjari 4. Sri Radha with Govinda, Gopinatha and Madana-mohana; Gauranga beside Govinda; Narottama and Lokanatha
html:
The coming of Sri Radhika to Govinda from Puri and of Radha-vinodini to Gopinatha; the new form of Radha brought by Jahnava; Srinivasa's studies with Sri Jiva and his explanation of the kadamba verse; how Mahaprabhu sent Kashishvara to serve Govinda and gave him His own Deity; Krishna Pandita; Lokanatha Gosvami and Narottama: service, vow and initiation

[p. 52]

1Bow down to Sri Krishna Chaitanya with His associates —
the limit of compassion, besides whom there is no other.

2Begging them Himself, He distributes the highest goal to the fallen;
the name "Purifier of the fallen" has now come true.

3Thus, beholding Madana-mohana, Gopinatha
and the others, (Srinivasa) deemed his life fulfilled.

4Beside Sri Madana-gopala and Sri Govinda
Sri Radhika-jiu had not formerly been manifest.

5Purushottama Jana, the son of Prataparudra,
hearing of this, was filled with compassion at heart.

6With great care, having wonderful (Deity) forms made,
he sent those incomparable ones.

7When they had come as far as Agra,
Madana-mohana started a play:

[p. 53]

8in a dream He speaks to the adhikari:
"Equip an escort and go quickly.

9Two Deities have been sent as Radhika;
but it is not so — no one knows the difference between them.

10The larger of the two is Lalita;
the smaller is Radha, full of beauty and virtues.

11By My order go and bring both;
place (Them) on the right and the left — so I tell you."

12Hearing of the wonder, the adhikari quickly went
and carefully carried out the order.

13Hearing this marvellous news, Bara-Jana
ponders in his mind what should be done.

14Meanwhile within the temple enclosure of the Moon of Nilachala (there was)
a most wondrous (Goddess) whom no one could understand.

15All knew Her as Lakshmi Thakurani;
service to Her, the all-enchanting, was performed behind the temple.

16Appearing in a dream, She commanded:
"I am Radha; send Me to Govinda."

17Receiving the command, overwhelmed with the bliss of prema,
he quickly sent Her to Govinda.

18Having performed a great abhisheka, they placed Her on the left;
incomparable is the beauty of Sri Radhika and Sri Govinda.1

19Beside Sri Gopinatha is Sri Radha-vinodini,
small in Her Deity form, all-enchanting.

[p. 54]

20When Sri Jahnava Thakurani came
to Vrindavana, she beheld all the Thakuras (Deities).

21Seeing that the Thakurani beside Gopinatha was small,
she then firmly resolved in her mind.

22Some days later, intoxicated with prema,
having returned to the land of Gaura,

23manifesting a most extraordinary form (of Radha),
she brought Her and settled Her beside Gopinatha.

24Having performed the abhisheka, they placed Her on the left,
and the former Thakurani they kept on the right.2

25Tasting moment by moment boundless sweetness,
intoxicated with the absorption of rasa, she was unaware of herself.

26For some days she herself cooked delicious dishes
and offered the bhoga daily with joy.

27So I have told of the three Thakuras,
hearing of whom is an elixir for devotees.

28How Mahaprabhu came to stand at Govinda's right
I shall relate further on.

29With Sri Jiva Gosani Acharya Thakura
began to study, without any pride.

30The Deity served by Sri Jiva's own hands is Radha-Damodara;
to Him, with Gosani's love, (Srinivasa) bowed down many times.

31Gosani's books, the explanations of the Sri Bhagavata and others,
the Rasamrita-sindhu and all the other works —

[p. 55]

32leaving aside only the times of bathing, chanting the mantra and eating,
he ceaselessly studied the books with tears in his eyes.

33As he reads, he sees the meaning come of itself;
from time to time he asks Jiva Gosani about the meaning.

34In a few years he read all the books
and came to know the whole essence of siddhanta and of rasa.

35Meanwhile one day Acharya Thakura
went to bathe on the bank of the Yamuna.

36Here, while Sri Jiva was teaching the Sri Ujjvala,
a question of siddhanta arose that could not be resolved:

37when Krishna went to Mathura, in Vraja, in Vrindavana,
the trees remained just as He had seen them;

38but at the gate of Vraja a kadamba sapling
Krishna had planted before He went to Mathura.

39That tree took root, and flowers opened on it;
bees and their mates eagerly drink the honey.

40Seeing this, the people of Vraja cannot keep life in their bodies:
"So long ago Krishna went away!" they conclude.

41Thus in the Srimad Ujjvala-nilamani, (in the chapter on) uddipana-vibhava: "Friend, the two-leaved (sapling) that the Lotus-eyed One planted at the gate of Vraja — this kadamba tree, now in bloom, torments the cowherd women."3

42As this was being explained together with qualified people,
waves of discussion rose in the ocean of separation.

[p. 56]

43Each speaks in his own way, but none can establish it;
Gosani ponders in his mind — no conclusion is reached.

44Meanwhile Sri Acharya Thakura arrived
and asks: "What is the discussion? Why has the midday (rite) not been done?"

45Then Gosani told him what the matter was;
hearing it, he smiled and spoke, having entered into the meaning of the shloka:

46"Just now one meaning has come to my mind."
Gosani says: "Speak, may it be flawless."

47Then Sri Acharya Thakura began to speak;
hearing only a hint of it, Gosani was overcome with prema.

48He said: "As Krishna saw all the trees,
so He began to contemplate them in His mind.

49Therefore all the trees remained as they were;
but the one He planted and left grows day by day.

50When the planted tree comes to His mind,
He thinks: 'Today the tree must be this big.'

51As Krishna contemplates, the tree grows:
it has blossomed, swarms of bees drink the honey."

52Hearing this explanation from Acharya Thakura's lips,
Gosani wept with everyone in amazement:

53"What Sri Gosani-jiu told me in a dream —
its visible fruit I have received today.

54I know: his mercy rests on you in full;
otherwise on whose tongue would such a meaning appear?"

[p. 57]

55The two bowed to each other and embraced in prema;
streams of tears from their eyes, thrills on their bodies.

56After some time, having bathed and so on,
both went to Govinda and partook (of prasada).

57Coming to his lodging, (Srinivasa) rested in his place;
he has no other business than studying the books.

58Gosani, reflecting, decided in his mind:
"He is worthy to be given the title 'Acharya':

59for he has reached the far shore of the siddhanta of rasa;
there is no book he cannot analyse.

60I shall wait a few more days;
if I can, I shall send him to the land of Gauda.

61Sri Gosani-jiu's order is to spread the books;
such fitness I see in no one else.

62What would be done through me will be done through him —
there is no doubt of it," he reflected in his heart.

63"But how, in separation from him,
shall I keep life in my body — this I cannot settle."

64Thus some days passed in reflection,
in study of the books and tasting the rasa of Krishna.

65Acharya Thakura comes to Bhatta Gosani
every day and offers dandavat obeisances.

66Some one service he always performs,
and then discusses the hidden siddhanta of rasa.

[p. 58]

67Again and again he is immersed in an ocean of bliss;
who saw it knows — who could describe it?

68The account of Mahaprabhu (standing) at Govinda's right,
mentioned before, I now set out in detail.

69When Sri Rupa manifested Govinda,
there was no adhikari — and he grew anxious.

70He sent a letter to Sri Mahaprabhu,
writing in it that (He) should send an adhikari.

71All the Gaudiyas who were in Nilachala
(the Lord) considered one by one in His mind.

72A disciple of Sri Ishvara Puri, most fortunate,
he is one of Mahaprabhu's chief associates,

73who always stays near Mahaprabhu —
that He would send him, who could have imagined?

74Calling Kashishvara, (Mahaprabhu) says: "Accept My word:
set out for Vrindavana to serve Govinda."

75As soon as he heard it, he began to weep;
he knows the order cannot be transgressed, and yet he spoke.

76He was ashamed and afraid to make a plea,
(but thought:) "If I do not speak I shall die; so I shall humbly ask:

77if for a moment I do not see Your lotus feet,
the world seems empty, my eyes go blind.

78How can You say all this to me?
I cannot understand it, and it gives me great pain."

[p. 59]

79Smiling, Mahaprabhu says: "What you have said is true.
(But) what is in My heart cannot be told just anywhere:

80what I am, that is Govinda — there is no difference at all.
Serve there with faith.

81If you wish to see Me in this form —
here, I give you My very Self: take it and go quickly."

82Saying this, a Deity of Gaurasundara
He lifted and lovingly placed in his hands:

83"This is I; you will always have My darshana;
whatever service you render I shall accept."

84Saying this, He embraced him again;
he bowed down and went off weeping.

85Some days later he arrived in Vrindavana
and came to where Rupa and Sanatana were.

86First of all he showed them Mahaprabhu's Sri Deity,
and afterwards told them everything.

87They beheld the all-enchanting Moon, Gauranga;
they were overcome with prema beyond restraint.

88Composing themselves with difficulty, they bowed down
and gave Kashishvara an incomparable welcome.

89At once they took him to Govinda;
having performed the abhisheka, they placed (Gauranga's Deity) at Govinda's right.4

90Even today that form is beside Govinda:
whoever is fortunate sees Him to his eyes' content.

[p. 60]

91Kashishvara served Govinda;
removing the bhoga, he offered camphor betel.

92Thus great festivals began;
that day, after the arati, they partook of prasada.

93Govinda's first adhikari — Kashishvara —
(was appointed by) Sri Rupa, with great joy at heart.

94Knowing (the Lord's) wish at heart, he always serves;
who can describe the countless forms (of his service)?

95Kashishvara Gosani is always intoxicated with great prema;
he cannot attend to all the details of the service.

96Especially when he thinks of Mahaprabhu's disappearance,
he himself does not know where he is.

97Knowing his heart, Rupa Gosani,
again and again asking his leave and consent,

98while Kashishvara was still present made Sri Krishna Pandita
adhikari of Govinda — this is known to the world.5

99Sri Krishna Pandita Gosani is an associate of Chaitanya,
by whose mercy the treasure of prema is obtained.

100When Sri Kashishvara Gosani withdrew (from this world),
Sri Acharya Thakura came to Sri Vrindavana.

101Krishna Pandita Gosani treated him as an equal;
there is no end to their friendship.

102With Sri Krishnadasa Kaviraja Gosani —
a respectful friendship, relishing the pastimes of Radha and Krishna.

[p. 61]

103When Sri Lokanatha Gosani came to Vrindavana,
he came and met Rupa and Sanatana.6

104As soon as he saw them both, he was overcome with prema
and, as one poor and lowly, bowed down.

105Both bowed to him, embraced him and rejoiced,
and showed him Gopala, Govinda and Gopinatha.

106Beholding Them, (he) thrilled, trembled, tears fell from both eyes;
of that bliss only one who saw it is witness.

107All knew him to be a great kulina brahmana
and urged him to perform (Deity) service.

108Seeing their great insistence, he served for some days,
but in his heart he was always overflowing with absorption in bhava.

109Unable to serve, he humbly declined
and was given a place north of Sri Radha-ramana —

110that place belongs to Sri Madana-gopala;
deeming it secluded, Mahashaya stayed there.

111Cooks and pujaris from three temples
bring him prasada — on that he lives.

112With Sri Rupa and Sanatana ceaselessly
he tastes the pastimes of Radha and Krishna with the highest joy.

113Thus some days passed;
absorbed in bhava, he noticed neither night nor day.

114Going to that Sri Lokanatha Gosani,
(Srinivasa) met him, bowing humbly.

[p. 62]

115He, delighted, embraced him with love;
there (Srinivasa) saw Sri Thakura Narottama.

116He bowed down to Acharya Thakura;
Acharya Thakura rose and embraced him.

117In both a natural love awoke;
gazing at each other, both attained the highest bliss.

118With tears, faltering, thrilled, Acharya Thakura
began to speak sweet words:

119"Has the Creator given me another eye today?
Or, giving me a hand, made me very glad?

120Or, giving me a wing, made me content?
Or pleased me with a priceless jewel?

121Or has he today given me my very life?
Or what bliss this is I cannot understand."

122Saying this, he embraced him again;
both bathed each other with tears.

123Seeing the conduct of Sri Lokanatha Gosani,
Acharya Thakura rejoiced greatly at heart.

124He is utterly detached and speaks with no one;
and if he says anything, it is in very sweet words.

125After relishing talk of Krishna for some time,
(Srinivasa) took leave and went away, bowing down.

126Sri Sanatana composed the Vaishnava-toshani;
in its mangalacharana are the sweetest words:

[p. 63]

127Gosani himself sings his (Lokanatha's) virtues;
as soon as they hear it, the hearts of all devotees melt.

128Thus (it is said): "I bow to those dear to Vrindavana who have taken shelter at Sri Govinda's feet — Srimat Kashishvara, Lokanatha and Sri Krishnadasa."7

129So also at the beginning of the Hari-bhakti-vilasa —
hearing it, the ears of those who have taken his shelter are soothed:

130"May the Sri Vaishnavas devoted to absolute bhakti here in the district of Mathura be victorious: Kashishvara, shining in Krishna's forest, Sri Krishnadasa, and that Lokanatha."8

131Thakura (Narottama) has great devotion to Acharya Thakura,
Acharya Thakura great love for Thakura.

132Once a day, going to (his) lodging,
(Narottama) leaves having received Acharya Thakura's darshana.

133Sometimes to Gosani (Lokanatha) Acharya Thakura
comes and, receiving his darshana, obtains great bliss.

134There the two meet;
thus, after talking of the Beloved (Lord), they part.

135How Thakura Narottama became Sri Lokanatha's disciple —
hear the account of it:

136Lokanatha Gosani does not accept disciples at all;
solitary, detached, and at the same time supremely rapt in bhava.

[p. 64]

137Especially after Sri Rupa Gosani's disappearance
his heart is always restless, and he says nothing to anyone.

138When Sri Thakura Narottama came to Vrindavana,
he beheld the places of the pastimes everywhere.

139The ocean of bliss at the darshana of even one place —
not one drop of it can be described in full.

140He had the desire to be initiated;
he looks everywhere and goes to everyone.

141When he saw Sri Lokanatha Gosani,
then and there he surrendered himself in his mind.

142Seeing his conduct and bearing, he cannot speak;
"How will this come about?" he constantly ponders.

143Night and day, going there unseen,
with tears in his eyes he does the outside work:

144he brings good earth for cleansing,
sprinkles, sweeps, brings water — various services.

145Every day, seeing this, Gosani is amazed:
"Whose piety is so great that he acts like this?"

146He tries to see (him) but cannot;
seeing this lowly service, his heart is full of compassion.

147Thus for some days he served;
and one day, as fate would have it, (Gosani) suddenly saw him:

148"Who are you? Why do you do such work?"
Weeping, Thakura speaks, full of fear and shame:

[p. 65]

149"I want only your favour, Prabhu;
show me this mercy — never forsake me."

150He says: "One thing — I do not accept disciples;
whatever else you ask, that I can do.

151By your service my heart has melted;
do this no more, spare me the embarrassment."

152Falling down and weeping, he says, (clasping) the Lord's feet:
"As soon as I saw (you), I surrendered myself.

153Whatever comes to your mind, do that:
you are my Lord, I am your servant."

154Hearing this, Gosani went away in silence;
and from the next day (Narottama) began to serve openly.

155Gosani never says anything to him,
and he does beforehand whatever (Gosani) might wish.

156Thus he served for about a year;
in what ways — it cannot be told.

157Then Gosani, devising a stratagem in his mind,
called Thakura and told him directly,

158knowing in his mind: "I shall tell him something
that he will in no way be able to do":

159"Hey, Narottama, accept one word of mine;
think it over and see whether you can do it.

160Then I shall initiate you;
otherwise do not speak to me of this again."

[p. 66]

161Thakura says: "Prabhu, whatever you say
is my duty — who would do otherwise?"

162Then he says: "Be detached from worldly things:
do not marry, do not eat parboiled rice or fish."9

163Hearing this, Thakura rejoiced
and fell down full length, clasping his feet.

164His body filled with thrills, he weeps with loud cries,
his whole body shakes, he cannot be still:

165"I shall do just that, Prabhu, which you have ordered.
Placing your foot on my head, say: 'Narottama is mine.'"

166Seeing his yearning, Gosani was amazed;
unable to hold back his tears, they flow down his breast.

167And, placing his foot on Thakura's head,
taking him on his lap, he speaks in great agitation:

168"I know: birth after birth you are my servant;
otherwise how could such anguish show itself?"

169Thakura says: "If you have been merciful to me,
give me the mantra of initiation, Prabhu — I cannot bear delay."

170Then, seated in the house, the procedure of initiation
he sets out in order, his heart overflowing with bhava.

171Giving the name of Hari, the mantra of Radha and Krishna, the five names,
he speaks of service, the goal and the path of sadhana.

172"Mahaprabhu, the son of Shachi, is the son of the king of Vraja" —
he set forth the extract, the essence of all siddhanta.

[p. 67]

173He gave him the siddha name Vilasa-manjari;
his own name he gave as Manjulali.10

174This much he told him briefly:
"Gradually you will obtain (knowledge of) it in detail."

175Thakura, remembering the mantra in solitude,
bowing to the guru, Krishna, the sadhus and Tulasi,

176in bliss fell and rolled on the ground;
bhava filled his whole body — it could not be contained.

177Thus after some time, growing calm,
he partook of Gosani's remnants.

178He stayed there and serves day and night,
pleasing Gosani with body, mind and word.

179Those whose all-in-all is Sri Rupa with his family —
for their joy this pastime is proclaimed.

180Wishing to describe this connection, the gurus and the rest,
Manohara Dasa tells the Anuraga-valli.

Thus ends, in the Srimad Anuraga-valli, in the description of the life of Srimad Acharya Thakura, the fourth manjari, called "The Fulfilled Desire of Sri Thakura Narottama".

Notes

  1. The tradition of Sri Radha sent from Puri by Purushottama Jana (son of Prataparudra), and of the Lakshmi of Jagannatha's temple who declared Herself Radha in a dream, is known from other biographies as well; in Manohara Dasa, of the two Deities sent, the smaller is Radha and the larger Lalita, both placed on either side of Madana-mohana.
  2. According to the Prema-vilasa (16), it was Madana-mohana who asked Jahnava for a form of Radha; in Manohara Dasa Jahnava brings Radha for Gopinatha, and the former Radha-vinodini stands on His right. "The land of Gaura" is Gauda.
  3. Ujjvala-nilamani, the chapter on uddipana-vibhava. Cf. Prema-vilasa 12: Srinivasa solves the riddle of the trees and creepers of Vrindavana in separation from Krishna and at once receives the title of Acharya from Jiva; in Manohara Dasa the question is different (the kadamba verse), and the title is given later (5.79).
  4. Cf. Bhakti-ratnakara 2.438–441: Mahaprabhu sends Kashishvara to Vrindavana and gives him the Deity of Gaura-Govinda, non-different from Himself. Here the occasion is Rupa's letter asking for a servant for Govinda. The Deity is not different from the Lord: "This is I" (83).
  5. Cf. Narottama-vilasa 2.243: after Kashishvara's departure Krishna Pandita serves Govinda; in Manohara Dasa Rupa appoints him while Kashishvara is still alive.
  6. According to the CC (Adi 10) and the Narottama-vilasa (1), Lokanatha came to Vrindavana at Mahaprabhu's order before Rupa and Sanatana; here the order is different.
  7. The mangalacharana of Sanatana Gosvami's Brihad-vaishnava-toshani (cf. Bhakti-ratnakara 1).
  8. Hari-bhakti-vilasa, one of the opening verses (cf. Bhakti-ratnakara 1).
  9. "Parboiled rice" (usha-chal) — rice treated with boiling water before husking. Lokanatha's conditions (celibacy, abstaining from such rice and from fish) and the year-long test are known only from the Anuraga-valli; in the Narottama-vilasa (2) Narottama is initiated for his diligent service, without conditions.
  10. As in the Prema-vilasa (11): Manjulali is Lokanatha's siddha form, Vilasa-manjari Narottama's.
